exact_mathlib_api.purpose: The fixed product reassociation preserves all jet norms, with no artificial inverse radius or parameter-scale factor.

findings: The same rootFlowParameterUnscale of the supplied Theta and delta is used; its parameterizedCircleInverse is composed with the original n01RootLabel. The fixed product reassociation is a linear isometry, mapping (0,0,theta) to ((0,0),theta). No new root flow or coordinate is chosen.

The actual stationary inverse equation yields G(0,0,theta)=label(theta). At order zero the odd monotone pi-lift displacement bound is applied; no bound on the unbounded raw angular coordinate is assumed.

Positive order outer jets are bounded using label displacement plus the actual identity jet, with a common inputLoss=max(labelLoss,flowLoss). Positive order inner jets are exactly those of the true circle inverse and have equal norms under reassociation.

The existing composition theorem chooses low order and output loss before functions or component indices and uses one high seminorm. Subtracting the angular projection adds at most one for every positive order; the larger output envelope absorbs this and the pi bound at order zero.

C0, low order, output loss and the order-indexed coefficient B all precede state, component, true host sample, side, root factor, qualitative strip radius, parameter normalization and selected flow. No inverse R or inverse delta appears in the estimate.
limitations: The same-component raw optical lower and genuine OrdinaryFlowJacobianBounds remain explicit conditional inputs. This review does not derive the missing optical certificate from current Through03.
The result concerns ordinary spatial root-axis jets. It does not yet prove even/odd physical extension jets, height jets, state SmoothDirections or the exact final N04c target.
